forensic_summary.trigger: The 'Tolerance Stack-up' Crisis. The physics of modularity collided with manufacturing reality when we attempted to scale the console to 80 faders (10 feet wide). The standard sheet metal tolerances (+/- 0.005") accumulated across the 5 independent chassis units, creating a 'Gap Failure' where the mounting holes for the 'Tie Plates' were misaligned by over 0.100", making assembly impossible.
forensic_summary.intervention: I executed a 'Brute Force' assembly protocol. I compressed a 2-month DFM campaign into 2.5 weeks, designing custom 'assembly jigs' at my home to avoid corporate tooling latency. I institutionalized the 'Ratcheting Strap' method—literally using a heavy-duty cargo strap to physically compress the independent steel chassis together, nullifying the tolerance stack-up before torque-ing the locking plates.
forensic_summary.result: This manual intervention salvaged the flagship launch, allowing us to ship the massive 80-fader configurations that defined the new 'ICON' industry standard. This product line effectively killed the large-format analog console market for film post-production.
